correctness.rationale: The normalized radial area measure gives squared monomial norms n!/(lambda)_n by the beta integral, hence the base kernel (1-z conj(w))^(-lambda). Evaluation at a is bounded, so the new norm is equivalent and the stated rank-one change can be checked directly by the reproducing property; the denominator is 1+hK_0(a,a)>0. Treating z and conj(w) as independent bidisk variables, the disk automorphism identity yields the scalar factor with u=phi_a(z)conj(phi_a(w)); the logarithmic difference is an integer multiple of 2pi i and is zero at (a,conj(a)), so fractional powers have the required branch throughout. Every |u|<1 is realized by a pair, and the nonzero prefactor does not affect zeros. The principal argument for 1-u is in (-pi/2,pi/2), so solving the logarithmic equation admits only actual angles 2pi k/lambda in that range, not arbitrary wrapped exponentials. The disk test reduces to rho<2cos(2pi k/lambda); since rho>1 this further restricts the actual angle to (-pi/3,pi/3). This gives exactly the strict mass thresholds, excludes boundary equality and justifies the ceiling count also when its input is integral. Roots cannot coincide within this angle range, and the scalar derivative is nonzero. Differentiating rho gives the stated strict decrease of squared modulus and the negative transverse derivative at entry. Each of the finitely many permitted integer indices enters at finite mass, giving saturation even when lambda/6 is integral. For fixed a,h, mu>=h forces log(rho)=O(1/lambda) and hence N/lambda tends to 1/3. At lambda=6 the derivative of lambda log(2cos(2pi/lambda)) is pi/sqrt(3); expansion and inversion give the proposed divergence. The bundled finite checker was inspected, not executed. Simplicity and counts concern scalar fibres rather than zero pairs or fixed-w slices.

evidence: Boudreaux constructs an equivalent weight with kernel zeros for an admissible weight; Perälä obtains zeros for suitable radial weight functions; Han–Qiu–Wang characterize completeness via bounded evaluation for positive Radon measures.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The first two are existence results in different classes or with freedom to choose a density, not uniform exact statements for the specified area-plus-one-atom family. The Radon-measure theorem can inform well-posedness but does not quantify zero counts, entry thresholds or multiplicities.

evidence: The concentrated-mass formula controls the unweighted case. The two-power density transition near (s,alpha)=(1,4) has boundary roots exp(±i pi/3), and Miña-Díaz represents kernels with products of Blaschke-factor powers as densities. Broad equivalent-weight existence constructs a weight, rather than classifying a class already fixed by an atomic prescription.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The classical rank-one and automorphism identities reduce the new problem to a scalar zero equation but neither a lambda=2 root calculation nor a density-phase result determines the branch-index cutoff, mass-divergence coefficient or large-lambda fibre count for all lambda. The tested claim requires exhausting the principal logarithm branch and analyzing geometric entry across the entire exponent and strength ranges, rather than taking a parameter specialization of those statements.

evidence: Resultary ec4368ab0a4e Finding and Proof Steps 1–2 gives the scalar kernel (1-t)^(-2)-kappa/(1+kappa)+E_{kappa,nu}(t) for concentrated rotation-invariant measures and explicitly allows singular measures. The error is zero at nu=delta_0. The proof obtains t=1±sqrt((1+kappa)/kappa).
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Matching the normalized area convention gives kappa=h=mu for alpha=0,a=0, so the interior negative root, threshold 1/3 and crossing coincide exactly. Centering by the standard disk covariance also reduces the rest of the unweighted slice to this case. Rotationally invariant unweighted measures near the center do not vary the base exponent lambda and do not yield the nonreal pairs at lambda>6.

originality.rationale: The earlier concentrated radial mass record contains the exact unweighted centered-atom kernel, threshold and crossing as its allowable delta_0 subcase. Under the usual disk covariance, this also supplies the unweighted slice for arbitrary a after rescaling the mass. The claims are not novel on that slice, nor for the rank-one tool or mere equivalent-norm existence of zeros. The prior comparison supports the distinct full continuous exponent diagram for the prescribed one-atom family, including the lambda>6 nonreal transition, all branch counts, exact entry and limiting laws; no inspected source gives that diagram or a broader result from which it directly follows. The categorical verdict is qualified by the bounded scope of the priority search.
residual_risks: The unweighted atom slice is demonstrably prior and is not credited as new.
Unindexed Uvarov-type or rank-one kernel literature could contain a broader exponent computation; the bounded comparison is not a historical certification.
The broad Deng–Huang–Qian hit was inspected only at its opening and was not used to exclude coverage in its full text.

value.rationale: A single positive evaluation penalty is a canonical singular change of a zero-free analytic Hilbert norm. The exact count and entry thresholds resolve, within that family, how much equivalent-norm change is needed to lose zero-freeness and when new nonreal fibres become possible. The continuously varying exponent yields a critical divergence, successive entries and an unbounded count law not present at the already-known unweighted atom. This classification is useful beyond showing existence or restating the rank-one identity.
